summary.intent: Execute and gap-close GSD phase 68.1 (wiring CipherBox's v2.0 web app onto the node/v3 read+write chain) through multiple rounds of wave-based parallel plan execution, verification, and live user bug reports, culminating in a passed verification and phase shipping.
summary.outcome: Phase 68.1 reached verification round 3 with status passed (5/5 success criteria, 2 human-approved deferral overrides); e2e suite improved from 11 failed/90 passed/107 not-run to 2 failed/205 passed/2 skipped, with all remaining failures being explicitly approved deferrals (recovery-tool v2/v3 mismatch, rotation-durability SC-4); three deferral todos were written and the user then invoked /ship-phase 68.1.

repo: CipherBox write-plane model: WriteChildRef is keyed by node UUID (childPub.id), never the ipnsName-based childId param used elsewhere — a recurring source of bugs when code conflates the two.
getWriteBodyParams fail-opens to {} when writeKey is zero (D-03), so any code path that loses/never-populates writeKey silently degrades to read-only publishing instead of erroring loudly.

TEE republish enrollment requires BOTH encryptedIpnsPrivateKey AND keyEpoch on POST /ipns/publish; createFolder previously omitted enrollment, meaning subfolder IPNS records were never durable (died at 48h TTL or on mock-ipns-routing restart).

mock-ipns-routing (dev delegated routing, :3001) keeps IPNS records in an in-memory Map wiped on every restart; production durability requires records to have both a DB row (ipns_records) and a republish_schedule row.

dfsFindFolder in client.ts previously always re-resolved and overwrote already-loaded ancestor folderTree entries on every call, contradicting its own 'later calls are cheap' docstring — root cause of breadcrumb-navigation flakiness.

moveItem only re-linked the read-plane SealedChildRef but left WriteChildRef orphaned in the source write-body — moving a file into a subfolder silently broke future edits (user-reported bug, fixed in 68.1-31).

Shared-folder writeKey seeding (68.1-20) only worked at share root depth; navigateToSubfolder seeded zero writeKey for nested folders, blocking deep shared writes (fixed in 68.1-30 via resolveSharedSubfolderWriteKey).

Direct single-file shares have no parent folder context, so the folder-based updateSharedFile path can't work for them — required a new updateSharedSingleFile SDK method targeting the file's own IPNS.

D-02 kind-cache is populated asynchronously in three separate projection sinks (folder.store SDK-event handler, handleSync, resyncFolder) — missing await-before-insert in any one causes files to render as folders (fixed across 68.1-14/15/33).

apps/web/public/recovery.html is v2-vault-blob-only and has never been updated since Phase 24, even though the app has produced v3/node-v3 blobs since Phase 62 — a real production gap, not a test issue.

shares table's plaintext item_name column was dropped by migration 1750000000000-ApiSchemaCutover, making the REQ-4 itemName backfill feature permanently dead code (GAP-6) — required as a deliberate product decision (retire + redesign encrypted) rather than a unilateral fix.
mock-ipns-routing healthcheck used busybox wget against 'localhost' which resolves to ::1, but the app binds IPv4-only — perpetual 'unhealthy' status was a healthcheck bug, not a service failure.

Local e2e requires API env vars TEST_LOGIN_SECRET=e2e-test-secret-do-not-use-in-production and DELEGATED_ROUTING_URL=http://localhost:3001; API listens on :3000, not :3001 (that's the delegated-routing mock).
tests/web-e2e specs use describe.serial per file, so a single early failure cascades and skips the rest of that file — raw failure counts understate real breakage until deep specs run to completion.

code.finding: getWriteBodyParams fails open to {} on zero writeKey, allowing silent write-body loss on publish.
moveItem re-homes WriteChildRef from source to dest write-body (68.1-31 fix); must key by resolved node UUID (childPub.id), not the ipnsName-based childId parameter.
Write-capability gate checks WriteChildRef presence by UUID — any re-homing/recovery logic must match this key.
updateSharedSingleFile added to support direct single-file-share writes without parent folder context (68.1-32).
Hybrid kind-cache projection: synchronous insert only when every child's kind is already cached; otherwise awaits resolveKinds with a stale-sequence guard (68.1-33).
handleSync bypasses SDK events entirely on FileBrowser mount and is the actual reload-gating inserter — needed its own resolveKinds-before-insert fix.
Previously hardcoded isFolder = true, ignoring the kind cache entirely in the shared browser (68.1-15 fix).

workflow: Background subagents driving long-running commands (full Playwright suites) frequently 'lose wake' — they park waiting on their own background shell and the completion notification never fires, requiring an independent disk-based watchdog plus SendMessage resume while the transcript is still warm.

When resuming a lost-wake or session-limit-killed agent, verify actual disk/git state first (uncommitted diffs, commit presence via git log) before trusting any self-reported summary or worktree_metadata (agents have misreported their own expected_base).
Decision-coverage gate for CONTEXT.md requires informational tags placed INSIDE the bold ID group (`- **D-04 [informational]:**`), not appended after it.
1Password git commit signing produces false-negative timeouts — always verify via `git log -1` before retrying rather than blind-retrying (which risks duplicate commits).

Worktree-isolated executors must never use git stash (shared refs/stash across worktrees can clobber other agents' or the user's stashed work) — this was violated twice this session and required manual recovery.

Live hands-on user testing surfaced three real bugs (cold-reload subfolder navigation, decryption failed in text editor, move-then-edit write-capability loss) that the e2e suite structurally could not reach due to serial-abort cascading — automation passing does not mean every code path was exercised.

A single gap round can spawn follow-up gap rounds recursively as fixing one blocker unblocks the next previously-unreachable test (10.3 fix exposed 10.4; move fix's frontier moved further each pass) — plan for iterative verification rather than a single pass.

friction: Two separate exit-gate agents lost their wake-up after launching long-running background e2e suites, requiring manual disk polling and SendMessage resumes.
Exit-gate agent died mid-session on the account session limit twice, requiring orchestrator-level inline recovery (validating diffs, fixing test harnesses, committing manually).

A background watchdog built to detect suite completion via .last-run.json never fired because this playwright config doesn't produce a usable file at that path — had to be manually stopped and replaced with direct log inspection.
Wrong cwd (stuck in `cd docker`) made ROADMAP.md appear missing, requiring a re-check from repo root.
index.lock contention transiently blocked a tracking commit, requiring verification that no partial commit had landed before retrying.
Two worktree-isolated executor agents ran the forbidden `git stash` command, requiring manual verification that only the intended stash entries were affected.

Test fixtures repeatedly went stale after production code changes (fileReadKey/fileWriteKey split, UUID node ids, mock call counts), causing post-merge gate failures that needed agent resumption to fix.
Full 208-spec Playwright suite takes ~20-25 minutes per run, and multiple rounds of full runs were needed as fixes landed incrementally — significant wall-clock cost per verification iteration.
mock-ipns-routing's healthcheck was misdiagnosed initially as a service failure; required probing inside the container to find the IPv6/IPv4 binding mismatch.
Web3Auth Core Kit login flakiness (external service) repeatedly muddied e2e failure triage, requiring single-file re-runs to distinguish real regressions from external flake.
